re_line: OPCON-as-withdrawal signal · Wang Yi briefs Seoul on Kim's Dandong visit · PPP Busan rally · DPRK naval buildup continues
morning_memo: US experts at a CSIS event assessed Trump views wartime OPCON transfer as a vehicle to withdraw US forces from Korea.
China's Wang Yi gave Seoul its most detailed account yet of Kim Jong Un's October 24 Dandong visit during FM-level talks.
People Power Party held a Busan street rally against the National Assembly-passed 'fabricated prosecution special counsel bill.'

key_stat.label: Binance funds DOJ moved to seize in North Korean crypto case
key_stat.context: The US Department of Justice moved to freeze nearly half of more than $6 billion stolen in North Korea's Binance hack, the largest single crypto-seizure action targeting Pyongyang.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed Nov 13 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: 38 North satellite imagery from October 16 confirms trucks traversing the New Yalu River (DPRK-Friendship) Bridge one day after the October 15 official opening, marking the start of commercial vehicle traffic. Daily NK reports (Oct 31) that North Korean trucks have still not joined Chinese cargo trucks on the bridge two weeks after the Oct 15 opening; North Korean transport officials are still preparing vehicles. North Korea-China trade reached $299M in September 2026, the second-highest monthly total in 2026. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reports on Nov 3, 2026 that North Korea is courting Chinese investors to build hotels and shopping complexes in Sinuiju. NK News reports a surge in North Korean delegations visiting China, putting commercial ties in focus. Daily NK reports Nov 12 that Chinese truck drivers who relied on side income ferrying parcels across the new bridge are souring on operations due to tighter customs checks and movement controls since the October opening. Huanghai Automobile's Dandong bus factory announced it is operating at full capacity on Nov 13 following Kim Jong Un's October visit, raising questions about potential vehicle exports to the DPRK.

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on Nov 4 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed Nov 6 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on Nov 3 and is under investigation.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed Nov 13 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.

top_stories.headline: Trump seen using OPCON transfer as path to US troop withdrawal, experts warn
China gives Seoul detailed account of Kim's Dandong visit; calls ties 'economic, not political'
top_stories.body: **Wang Yi** elaborated on Kim Jong Un's October 24 visit to Dandong during talks with **FM Cho Hyun** in Beijing on November 13, with a South Korean official saying China described its North Korea relationship as focused on economic cooperation rather than political affairs. The official assessed a US-North Korea summit as possible but not highly likely, saying it would depend on US President Donald Trump's willingness. Cho called on China to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue.

also_today.headline: Kim Jong Un remakes North Korea's flag, ditching Soviet-era design
also_today.body_text: WSJ reports Kim Jong Un has formally modified North Korea's national flag, breaking from the Soviet-era design embedded in the revised constitution published earlier this month. The flag change was formalized alongside broader constitutional revisions that expanded Kim's powers and codified the two-state framework.

also_today.headline: DOJ freezes nearly half of $6B stolen in North Korea's Binance hack
also_today.body_text: The US Department of Justice said it helped freeze nearly half of more than $6 billion stolen in North Korea's Binance hack, moving to seize $1.2 billion in funds. The action follows an FBI report that North Korean hackers stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over the last 18 months.

also_today.headline: Kim Jong Un inspects second major east-coast naval base, orders timely completion
also_today.body_text: Kim Jong Un inspected a second major east-coast naval base under construction on November 12-13, ordering completion on the schedule and to the quality standard set by the party central. NK News separately identified the second base project beyond the Munchon-area site Kim first visited on November 12.

also_today.headline: US nationwide flight halt delays Incheon departures to New York, Atlanta, Boston
also_today.body_text: A US Federal Aviation Administration nationwide ground stop caused by air traffic control communications problems delayed Incheon flights to New York, Atlanta and Boston by approximately two hours Saturday. The FAA said the outage affected 22 regional air traffic control centers; US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin indicated no evidence of malicious activity.

also_today.headline: Iran warns South Korea over expanded naval mission
also_today.body_text: Iran issued a warning to South Korea over an expanded ROK naval mission, according to Dong-a Ilbo. The warning comes as Seoul has maintained a naval presence in waters relevant to Mideast security operations.

also_today.headline: What's Behind South Korea's Rift With Ukraine and Turn Toward Russia?
also_today.body_text: Carnegie Politika traces Seoul's diplomatic rupture with Kyiv to the September 23 UN General Assembly dispute over North Korean prisoners of war, culminating in Seoul recalling its ambassador from Ukraine on October 8. The piece notes signs of South Korean reengagement with Russia but identifies limits to how far the foreign-policy shift will go.

rok_government.action: Cho meets Wang Yi in Beijing; urges China to bring North Korea back to dialogue
rok_government.detail: FM Cho Hyun met Chinese FM Wang Yi in Beijing on November 13 for approximately three hours of talks and dinner, the first ministerial meeting in about three months. Cho stressed that peninsula peace serves shared interests and called on China to play a constructive role; Wang reaffirmed Beijing's unchanged Korea Peninsula policy and welcomed President Lee's planned APEC attendance in Shenzhen.

rok_government.detail: Korea has pursued the agreement with Nepal since 2024.

rok_government.action: Industry minister assures Czech counterpart Czech nuclear project on schedule; regular ministerial consultations to begin
rok_government.detail: Industry Minister Kim Jeong-gwan told his Czech counterpart that the Czech nuclear plant project will proceed on schedule without disruption and agreed to activate a regular ministerial-level consultative body, with a first session before year-end.

calendar_watch.headline: Hudson Institute event: Overcoming US-ROK Alliance Challenges
calendar_watch.detail: Hudson Institute hosts a panel titled 'Overcoming US-ROK Alliance Challenges: Trade, Technology, and China' on November 17.

rok_assembly.action: National Assembly passes 'fabricated prosecution special counsel bill'
rok_assembly.detail: The ruling Democratic Party drove passage of the so-called 'fabricated prosecution special counsel bill' through the National Assembly plenary on November 14, triggering a major PPP rally in Busan. PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk called the bill 100 percent unconstitutional and demanded a presidential veto.

us_korea_deals.state_of_play: Steel and aluminum remain at 50% and automobiles at 15%, both under Section 232. The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, so there is no baseline reciprocal tariff in force. Section 301 investigations, launched March 11 against 16 trading partners including South Korea, are now the primary prospective tariff vehicle.

trade_policy.detail: Samsung and SK Hynix China fabs operating under annual BIS export licenses renewed December 30, 2025 for 2026; maintenance and incremental upgrades only, no expansion. Shifted from indefinite VEU waivers to restrictive annual licenses January 2026.

Foreign Entity of Concern rules affect Korean EV battery makers (LG Energy Solution, SK On, Samsung SDI) sourcing from China; battery components phase-in December 2024, critical minerals December 2025.

business_economy.headline: US Treasury Secretary blames Commerce for failure to sanction Nvidia chip-diversion suspect Megaspeed
business_economy.body_text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department for not blacklisting Singaporean firm Megaspeed, suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China, saying Treasury, State, Defense and USTR all agreed months ago to add it. Bessent said Trump had been clear China must not receive Nvidia chips beyond the A100 level, and that the authority to enforce already exists.

business_economy.headline: South Korea lays groundwork for homegrown Starlink satellite constellation
business_economy.body_text: South Korea is developing the foundational infrastructure for a domestic satellite internet constellation analogous to Starlink, Dong-a Ilbo reports. The initiative reflects Seoul's push for strategic communications autonomy.

northeast_asia.headline: Cho-Wang Yi talks: Seoul requests constructive Chinese role on North Korea; FTA services talks to advance
northeast_asia.body_text: Cho also raised the West Sea (Yellow Sea) issue and protection of Korean nationals in China.

northeast_asia.headline: South Korea seeks EU exemptions for steel, nuclear equipment
northeast_asia.body_text: Seoul is pursuing European Union exemptions for Korean steel exports and nuclear equipment, UPI reports, as part of broader efforts to diversify trade policy relief following US Section 232 tariff pressure.

northeast_asia.headline: South Korea holds separate Sado mine memorial, pressing Japan on historical record
northeast_asia.body_text: South Korea held a separate memorial ceremony for Korean victims of the Sado mine, maintaining pressure on Japan to fully acknowledge the history of wartime forced labor at the UNESCO World Heritage site.

rok_personnel.name: William Daley
rok_personnel.detail: William Daley was named Chair of the CSIS Board of Trustees. Paul Ryan was named Vice Chair.

official_x_posts.quote_text: Met again with Chinese FM Wang Yi in Beijing three months after our August meeting in Korea, discussing Korea-China relations and Korean Peninsula issues over talks and dinner. We discussed creating concrete outcomes in Korea-China relations that our citizens can feel. President Lee will attend the Shenzhen APEC summit in a few days; I will work until the last moment to make this visit an important occasion for developing Korea-China relations.
official_x_posts.analyst_note: The post confirms the November 13 ministerial as Beijing's pre-APEC diplomatic preparation ahead of a planned Lee-Xi bilateral on the summit sidelines.

opeds_today.headline: William Daley and Paul Ryan Named Chair and Vice Chair of the CSIS Board of Trustees
opeds_today.central_argument: CSIS has named William Daley as Board Chair and Paul Ryan as Vice Chair, reshaping the leadership structure of the institution that runs the Korea Chair.
opeds_today.summary: CSIS announced the appointment of William Daley as Chair and Paul Ryan as Vice Chair of its Board of Trustees. The leadership change affects the institution that houses the Korea Chair and several other flagship programs. No Korea-specific programmatic changes were announced alongside the leadership transition.

opeds_today.source: CSIS | Center for Strategic and International Studies
opeds_today.headline: China and Russia's Role in North Korea's Human Rights Abuses | The Capital Cable #79
opeds_today.central_argument: China and Russia bear direct responsibility for enabling North Korea's human rights abuses.
opeds_today.summary: The piece examines the roles China and Russia play in North Korea's human rights abuses.

kcna_delta.kim_activity: Kim Jong Un inspected a second major east-coast naval base under construction on November 12-13, ordering that it be completed on the schedule and to the quality standard set by the party central.

top_articles.headline: North Korea faked November 4 cluster warhead test using doctored photos from 2022
top_articles.summary: NK News reports that North Korea's November 4 announced cluster warhead test was fabricated using doctored imagery from 2022, adding to a pattern of domestic weapons-test blackouts.

key_quotes.speaker: Kim Jong Un
key_quotes.quote: Modern naval base construction is a major core project directly linked to our state's safety and defense of maritime sovereignty, and must unconditionally be completed within the period decided by the party central and at the quality level demanded by the party central.
key_quotes.context: KCNA report, Nov 13, inspection of east-coast naval base under construction
key_quotes.source_article: N. Korea's Kim inspects east coast naval base under construction, urges timely completion

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media led with Kim's second consecutive east-coast naval base inspection; NK News separately reported the November 4 cluster warhead test was fabricated using 2022 imagery.

capitol_hill.headline: US House passes small business protection bill targeting North Korean and other foreign threats
capitol_hill.body_text: The US House passed a bill to shield small businesses from foreign threats including North Korea, according to VOA Korean service. The measure addresses cybersecurity and economic security vulnerabilities at the small-business level.

capitol_hill.headline: China's access to Nvidia chips in doubt as export curbs gain traction in US Congress
capitol_hill.body_text: Congressional momentum for tighter Nvidia chip export controls to China is growing following the Jensen Huang scandal, with bipartisan interest in restricting advanced AI chip flows. The Korea Times notes Korean chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix could face secondary effects on their China fab operations.

korea_world.headline: KHNP reviews Czech nuclear project progress with local client
korea_world.body_text: Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power (KHNP) reviewed progress on the Czech nuclear project with its local client, as Industry Minister Kim Jeong-gwan separately assured his Czech counterpart the project would proceed on schedule with a regular ministerial-level consultative channel activated before year-end.

korea_world.headline: Kia plans to invest $2 billion in second plant in India
korea_world.body_text: Kia plans to invest $2 billion in a second manufacturing plant in India, Korea Herald reports, deepening the South Korean automaker's presence in one of the world's fastest-growing auto markets.

korea_world.headline: Malaysia to receive all 18 FA-50M fighter jets from South Korea by March 2028
korea_world.body_text: Malaysia's defense minister confirmed all 18 FA-50M light combat aircraft ordered from South Korea will be delivered by March 2028. The FA-50M contract is part of Seoul's growing defense export portfolio in Southeast Asia.
